automations.prompt:
Produce Syncranicity LLC's daily national electric-land deep scan. Use the August 31, 2026 operating doctrine as the framework, with the revised rules: all 50 states in scope, rural/open-land prior, $5,000 learning cap, $10,000 cumulative soft-control cap on the one live paid parcel, one primary plus two unpaid backups, Model A founder-led Stage 2, public-evidence-first buyer intelligence, seller-motivation analysis, alternate-use downside analysis, aggressive collection and conservative killing. Review current primary/public data and the live Syncranicity node-scout endpoint at https://syncranicity.vercel.app/api/node-scout?limit=250. Each day: (1) deeply review at least two states on a rotating basis so every state is revisited regularly; (2) identify material EIA, utility, transmission, generation, tariff, commission-docket, planning, political, water, environmental, fiber/logistics, parcel/listing, seller-motivation, and buyer/developer changes; (3) update revealed-preference buyer dossiers from recent acquisitions, options, deeds, leases, permits, utility agreements, filings, financing and project announcements; (4) identify promising NODE_LEAD_ONLY candidates but never infer available MW; (5) identify the cheapest next falsification for each promoted lead; (6) separate hard kill, soft kill, hold, and save-for-catalyst candidates; (7) analyze plausible alternate uses and downside floor before recommending control; (8) surface founder-dependent actions only when they unlock a decision; and (9) keep external outreach, spending, contracting and legal/engineering conclusions human-approved. Deliver a concise daily report containing: material changes; top three node leads or 'none'; buyer-intelligence changes; seller-motivation opportunities; two-state deep-dive findings; killed/held leads and why; exact founder actions for the day; and any source/data failures. Treat EIA generation capacity as generation data, not load-serving capacity.

September 5, 2026 operational amendment. These rules supersede conflicting research-category or GIS-sequencing rules above; retain the existing national rotation and other nonconflicting responsibilities:

Research electricity-intensive land opportunities for Syncranicity LLC across all 50 states, favoring open/rural land and realistically closable opportunities. Preserve the existing national rotation, cadence, alert settings, free-first data policy and source coverage. Collect broadly and detect changes aggressively, but distinguish signals from parcel-specific evidence and kill conservatively. Keep one live paid-control position plus two unpaid backups, the $5,000 learning cap, and $10,000 cumulative soft-control exposure cap. Do not authorize spending or contacting counterparties.

### Stage A: discovery and cheap initial screening

Create or update a basic record for every substantive candidate: stable source/record ID, APN or offered-tract identifier if known, state/county, actual governing jurisdiction if known, location precision, reported acreage/price and dates, original source, electricity/utility signal, buyer/use hypothesis, obvious known restrictions, ordinary alternate-use hypothesis, uncertainties and the cheapest decisive next test. Separate a generating-plant point, broad search area, parent parcel, offered portion, individual APN and multi-APN opportunity.

Apply the existing approved screening gates. Promote only when there is a traceable parcel/offering and resolved county, plausible scale/use/control economics and buyer fit, an attributable infrastructure/utility-process signal, no sufficiently supported fatal defect, and an inexpensive next verification. Remaining capacity/title/permit unknowns must be visible; expensive formal utility evidence is not required merely to prioritize research. Candidates that cannot yet be located or defined remain unresolved, not invented parcels.

### Stage B: three research categories

PRIORITY: initial-screen survivors. Immediately queue deep county-GIS review. Use substatuses GIS_QUEUED, GIS_IN_PROGRESS, GIS_REVIEWED, GIS_BLOCKED and HUMAN_VERIFICATION_NEEDED. This category expresses research priority, not investment clearance.

WATCH / DEVELOP: unresolved, weaker, curable or catalyst-dependent leads. Preserve useful basic research and a next catalyst. Do not run exhaustive county-GIS review routinely.

REJECTED / LEARNING: a supported rejection of a site, claim or current business strategy. Preserve the distinction. Retain reason, source/evidence date, confidence, money/time if known, what could have caught the problem earlier, lesson, and reopening condition. Do not routinely deep-scan archived sites. Missing/blocked evidence alone is HOLD, not proof of fatal infeasibility.

Do not silently reopen human-archived records. A narrowly scoped recheck to assess a documented new catalyst is allowed; full county review begins only after re-promotion. Do not delete older research. Keep prioritization, investigation stage, evidence confidence and capital authorization as different fields.

### Stage C: official county GIS deep review — PRIORITY ONLY

1. Resolve the county from the actual parcel, not the listing's nearest city. Open the official county site, its GIS/assessor/planning pages and linked map portals. Identify city/township authority where applicable. Verify provenance of externally hosted services.
2. Inspect the actual layer inventory, legend, parcel popups and map, and/or lawful published GIS services and downloads. Merely finding a portal link is not an investigation.
3. Retrieve the exact APN polygon and offered portion where possible. Check boundary currency, CRS, offered-parent differences, acreage discrepancies and multi-parcel assembly.
4. Review base zoning, future land use, mapped overlays/special districts, pending cases and restrictions; public/private roads, road ROW/dedication/maintenance/access; mapped easements, plats/deeds and road instruments; flood/floodway/drainage; wetlands, slope/soil; water/service districts; aviation/military, historic/conservation and other relevant local overlays; nearby incompatible uses. Identify the underlying code or recorded instrument needed to interpret each material map signal.
5. Use whole-polygon intersections when geometry permits; query full pages/results and verify coverage. A centroid or point query does not clear the property. Report FOUND, NO_FEATURE_IN_COVERED_QUERY, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_REVIEWED, BLOCKED, CONFLICT or NEEDS_INTERPRETATION accurately.
6. Save publisher, source URL, layer ID/name, effective/retrieval dates, CRS, query extent/geometry, result completeness/counts, relevant map capture or exported features where permitted, and proof limits. Keep source errors and known gaps. Respect usage terms/rate limits and access controls.
7. Distinguish road depiction from legal access, and mapped easements from complete title. Do not assume the absence of a layer means the absence of a restriction. Do not infer buildable acreage from advertised gross acres. When feasible, separate gross/GIS/scenario-net/largest-contiguous area; validate geometry and subtract unions rather than double-counting overlapping constraints. Label assumed buffers as scenarios.
8. Reassess the candidate after review. Retain Priority, downgrade to Watch, propose a supported rejection, or record GIS_BLOCKED with a precise next step. Never force a favorable verdict to fill the top category.

### Evidence and output rules

Use versioned approved requirement weights and transparent research-priority scoring. Scores are not calibrated close probabilities. Preserve inherited source dates and uncertainty. Current official GIS may substantiate a published map fact without proving title, surveyed dimensions, data-center permission or utility deliverability. Keep available load MW UNKNOWN without exact-load/exact-parcel utility evidence; generation capacity, voltage and infrastructure proximity do not establish it.

Calls follow desktop research and target only the remaining decision-sized gap: identify APN, source/layer or instrument, discrepancy, precise question, responsible office/contact, decision unlocked and cost estimate. Do not place calls, submit requests, email, order studies or bind the company automatically. Buyer fit is inferred from attributable public acquisitions/leases/options/permits and prior behavior, not invented mandates or unsolicited buyer interviews.

Every run reports: material changes; ranked Priority candidates and why they passed the initial screen; county-GIS findings and source failures for the Priority queue; concise Watch/Rejected updates; unresolved questions and next founder actions; and source coverage. If no candidate qualifies, say so. Record the remaining queue when deep research exceeds the run's available capacity; do not label unprocessed work completed. Reuse county metadata and unchanged findings while preserving freshness and revisit triggers.

Persist through the tested authorized research-ingestion route when one exists. Include producer/task ID, run ID, record/opportunity/APN IDs, produced/retrieved times, original report, structured findings, citations, changed fields, before/after category, reason and next action. Verify the durable write and readback; repeat delivery must not duplicate records or overwrite founder decisions. If no supported write route exists, return a structured report for authenticated import and explicitly mark the delivery UNSYNCED / MANUAL_INGESTION_REQUIRED. Do not claim automatic website updates from merely producing a chat response. Do not assume scheduled tasks can access project attachments, browser-local storage or this handoff ZIP.

Use $electric-land-deal-engine in this conversation to identify new or materially changed likely buyers for my Arizona large-load origination and predevelopment service.

Business context: I am building a demand-first service that creates buyer-specific, transferable development certainty for electricity-intensive projects—not a generic land-report business. My offer can include exact parcel candidates, seller authorization or conditional control, verified serving-utility intake readiness, and a documented zoning, water/cooling, fiber, access, political, and diligence path. Treat a 10–25 MW first phase with a credible 50 MW expansion path as the initial hypothesis unless current buyer evidence supports a different requirement.

On each run:
1. Review prior findings in this conversation and deduplicate them. Do not repeat unchanged coverage or reopen rejected leads without new evidence.
2. Search current primary sources first, then reliable trade sources, for dated demand signals: company releases and filings; expansion, financing, acquisition, lease, power-contract, utility-service, permitting, zoning, economic-development, and land-control activity; executive and site-team hiring; utility or regulator dockets; and delayed, failed, or cancelled projects that may create a relocation need.
3. Prioritize customer classes that are likely to buy external origination help: sponsor-backed merchant developers; vertically integrated AI/HPC or data-center operators expanding into new markets; national site-selection, engineering, brokerage, and development firms lacking Arizona coverage; and out-of-state large-load operators entering secondary markets. Include hyperscalers only when evidence indicates a specific external-vendor, origination, or geographic gap.
4. Rank each lead on near-term expansion evidence, Arizona or Southwest fit, plausible load/phase fit, capital and execution credibility, likely need for outsourced local origination, urgency, accessibility of the decision function, and fit with my service. Do not infer interest in any parcel.
5. For each new or materially changed lead, report: company; buyer segment; dated trigger; target geography; official MW/load if stated, otherwise unknown; why the company may need this service; likely decision-maker function or title; evidence class V0–V4; direct source links and retrieval date; confidence and disqualifiers; recommended outreach angle; and the single next founder action. Verify any contact channel on the day it is recommended; never invent a person, address, phone number, MW figure, timeline, or intent.
6. Organize the update as New priority leads, Material changes, Watchlist, No-action removals, and Today's founder actions. For the top one to three actionable leads, include a concise outreach message and the discovery questions needed to validate buyer requirements.
7. Separate observed facts from inference. Treat voltage, infrastructure proximity, announcements, hiring, or utility territory as signals—not proof of available power, buyer commitment, or parcel fit. Date mutable facts and link the strongest source.
8. Do not message anyone, sign anything, represent facts externally, spend money, or commit me to a transaction. Default authorized spend is $0.
9. If there is no meaningful new or changed buyer signal, do not notify me.
